correctness.rationale: For finite \(I\), the proof exactly rewrites the two shifted \(\ell_1\) norms using \(u_i=\min(|x_i|,|y_i|)\) and the two sign classes. It proves \(\min\{A,B\}=2-2\max\{P,N\}\) and then \(\max\{P,N\}\ge m(x)\); together with \(\max\{A,B\}\le2\) and monotonicity of \(M_t\), this yields the sharp upper bound for every parameter. A coordinate vector at a minimum-modulus coordinate attains equality. For infinite \(I\), coordinate moduli have infimum zero, so explicit coordinate-vector witnesses converge to the universal upper bound \(2\). Boundary cases \(t=0\) and \(t=-\infty\) are handled by the defining continuous conventions. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The defining 2023 article was inspected in full. It defines the pointwise James type family, gives global \(\ell_p\) values, and proves a finite-dimensional extreme-point reduction only for \(t\ge1\), but it does not state the pointwise \(\ell_1\) coordinate formula or the infinite-index collapse. Semantic searches for the formula, its smallest-coordinate formulation, the infinite \(\ell_1\) collapse, and possible equivalences returned no covering result. The closest published result treats pointwise \(\ell_p\) only for \(2<p<\infty\). The 2004 pointwise-nonsquare paper is a residual endpoint risk because only its abstract was accessible, but its stated object predates and is narrower than the full power-mean family; even complete overlap at \(t=-\infty\) would not imply the unified all-parameter theorem.
residual_risks: The full text of Tang–Ji–Wang (2004) was unavailable; it may contain the \(t=-\infty\) specialization under older pointwise-nonsquare terminology.

value.rationale: The result completely classifies a natural pointwise geometric invariant on the classical space \(\ell_1(I)\) across its entire parameter range. In finite dimensions it identifies the exact controlling statistic, the full value range, and both equality loci; in infinite dimensions it gives an all-point collapse to the maximal value. This goes beyond recomputing a global constant and fills a direct gap left by the defining article, whose practical finite-dimensional reduction is restricted to \(t\ge1\).
